notes: Sourced from Crown's official DCi Series - Network Input Models Operation Manual (Harman/Crown Audio, doc #5040450, rev 02/15), page 7 "Back Panel Features (2|300N, 2|600N, 2|1250N, 4|300N, 4|600N, 4|1250N, 8|300N, 8|600N)" — this back panel layout is explicitly shared by, and labeled as applicable to, the 8|300N. Cross-checked against Crown's product page (crownaudio.com/en-US/products/dci-8-300n) and B&H/Full Compass/Vintage King listings. All 4 input-pair and 4 output-pair connectors are physically identical repeated euroblock/Phoenix-style pluggable terminal blocks (6-pin for inputs, 4-pole for outputs); third-party parts references confirm Euroblock/Phoenix part P/N 5024623 for inputs. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the GPIO port is physically a 6-position RJ-11 telephone-style modular jack per the manual, NOT an RJ45 — RJ-11 is not present in the supplied connector enum, so "rj45" was substituted as the closest available modular-jack id; treat this single port's connector field as an approximation, not a literal match. AC inlet is confirmed 15A IEC C14 specifically for the 8|300N (the higher-power 8|600N in the same chassis instead uses a 20A IEC inlet — only the 8|300N's 15A rating is reported here). Ethernet control-port link speed (10/100 vs Gigabit) is not stated anywhere in the manual or Crown's marketing pages, so grade was omitted for it; the two BLU link ports were graded eth-1g because the manual explicitly states BLU link is "Based on Gigabit Ethernet technology" run over Cat5e cabling (100m per hop), though BLU link is a proprietary audio bus/ring rather than routable Ethernet. Confidence is "high" given the primary source is Crown's own authoritative operation manual with a labeled rear-panel diagram; the RJ-11-as-rj45 substitution and the unstated Ethernet control-port speed are the two open caveats.

ports.name: GPIO
ports.note: Physical connector is actually a 6-position RJ-11 jack (not RJ45) — RJ-11 is not in the allowed connector enum, so rj45 (closest modular-jack family match) was used as a placeholder. 2 analog/binary inputs + 2 binary outputs for preset recall, volume control, etc. No grade applies; this is a low-voltage control port, not a data-network link.
